newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar weakens against yen by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar weakens against yen by late Tokyo.

text.p: 0633 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar weakened against the yen by late Tokyo as exporters' offers and sales by interbank traders above 116.80 yen checked its gains.

The greenback underwent a downward correction in the morning on a vague, unconfirmed rumour that senior Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara said the yen may strenghten to 103 yen to the dollar, dealers said.
The rumour could not be confirmed. Some traders said it was probably just talk by traders to improve their dollar positions.

Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, told a parliamentary committee in the afternoon that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) and the Finance Ministry are keeping in close contact on currencies and will maintain such contacts in the future.
But he did not mention currency levels in his remarks.
A trust bank dealer said Tokyo operators started selling dollars as they saw 117 yen as a short-term ceiling. Dealers detected steady exporter offers above 116.80 yen.

But a city bank dealer said: "After seeing a strong U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index (on Monday), I think the dollar will be bought further in overseas trade later today."
Dealers said they were waiting for Friday's U.S. jobs data to make a further judgment on a possible U.S. rate rise.

Meanwhile, expectations of an imminent credit-tightening in Japan were dimmed by comments by Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita, who told a parliamentary committee on Tuesday that the current low interest rate policy is helping Japan's economic recovery, dealers said.

The mark's weakness continued against the dollar and yen amid wariness over broader EMU and a weak euro, along with the German government's conflict with the Bundesbank over the possible revaluation of its gold reserves, dealers said.

"The market is looking at weakness in the European currencies rather than strength in the dollar," a bank dealer in Singapore said, adding that the French election results had contributed to this trend.
The dollar rose as high as 1.7333 marks in Tokyo before long-liquidation sales ate away earlier gains. The mark fell as low as around 67.15 yen and remained weak in cross trade.
The bank dealer in Singapore said dollar/mark remained on an uptrend with support expected around 1.7200.
Japanese investors' hedge sales of marks for yen also dragged the mark/yen rate down amid uncertainty over European economic and monetary union (EMU), dealers said.
But another trust bank dealer said he wanted to see the lineup of the new French cabinet in order to get further clues to France's stance on EMU.
The dollar closed at 116.55/65 yen and 1.7290/00 marks in New York on Monday. --- Singapore newsroom +65-8703080
--- Yoko Nishikawa in Tokyo +81-3-3432-8584
